property_summary: setL1BlockValues reverts for callers whose address is not equal to C.DEPOSITOR_ACCOUNT (i.e., only the depositor can call successfully).

For every call to setL1BlockValues, the contract's public 'number' equals the uint64 _number argument passed; the mutant assigns _timestamp into number instead, so for inputs where _number != _timestamp the mutant breaks this property.
For every call to setL1BlockValues(...) the contract's public getter number() equals the provided _number; the mutant that assigns number = 0 breaks this rule for any _number != 0.

For any call to setL1BlockValues by the depositor, the contract's public `number` equals the calldata `_number` (i.e., the stored number is overwritten to exactly the provided _number); the mutant that adds to the existing number instead causes `number` to differ for inputs where prior number != 0 or when _number != previous value.

For any input to setL1BlockValues, the reference contract sets number exactly to the provided _number (overwrite); the mutant that increments instead causes number != _number for some inputs (when prior stored number != 0), so the property is that after calling setL1BlockValues, c.number() == the _number argument.

For any single call to setL1BlockValues from the authorized depositor, the reference contract's stored number equals the calldata _number when the prior stored number is zero; the mutant that adds to the existing number will make c.number() != _number when prior number is non-zero, so calling twice where the first call sets a non-zero prior and the second provides any _number will reveal the bug (the reference still sets number to the second call's _number).

For any depositor-provided _number and prior state, a single call to setL1BlockValues by the authorized depositor sets C.number() equal to the provided _number (overwrite); the mutant that increments breaks this when prior number != 0 by making C.number() equal prior+_number instead.

Rule: Only the designated DEPOSITOR_ACCOUNT can successfully call setL1BlockValues (so number changes only when msg.sender == DEPOSITOR_ACCOUNT); the mutant also allows address(this) (self-calls) so a self-call can change number — violating the rule for some inputs where the contract calls itself.

For any inputs sent by the depositor, the contract's timestamp public getter equals the provided _timestamp argument after setL1BlockValues is called; the mutant that ignores the parameter and sets timestamp = uint64(block.timestamp) can violate this when _timestamp != block.timestamp.

For any caller equal to DEPOSITOR_ACCOUNT and any inputs, calling setL1BlockValues sets the public timestamp to the provided _timestamp; the mutant ignores _timestamp and sets timestamp to zero, violating this rule for inputs where _timestamp != 0.

For any inputs and when setL1BlockValues completes successfully, the reference contract always sets timestamp to the provided _timestamp (i.e., c.timestamp() == _timestamp); the mutant that assigns timestamp last can leave timestamp unchanged when a revert (from elsewhere) occurs before that assignment, breaking this property for some inputs.

For any call to setL1BlockValues by the depositor, the correct contract always sets timestamp to the supplied _timestamp when the call completes; the mutant that moves the timestamp assignment last can leave timestamp unchanged if a later assignment or external check causes a revert before timestamp is written, so there exist inputs (fuzzer-discovered) where timestamp differs.

For every successful call to setL1BlockValues by the depositor, the reference contract always sets timestamp to the provided _timestamp; the mutant that assigns timestamp last can leave timestamp unchanged when a subsequent operation reverts, so there exist inputs (a depositor call that triggers a revert after other assignments) for which the mutant's timestamp differs.

For any call by the depositor that completes without reverting, the reference contract always results in c.timestamp() equal to the supplied _timestamp; the mutant that moves the timestamp assignment to the end can produce a revert in a later operation (when interacting with an adversarial batcherHash callee) causing the call to revert before timestamp is set, so there exist fuzzed inputs (a batcherHash that is a contract whose fallback reverts) for which the mutant fails to set timestamp while the reference would have already set it.

For any call to setL1BlockValues made by the depositor, the correct contract always sets timestamp to the supplied _timestamp by the time the external call returns; the mutant that moves the timestamp assignment to the end can leave timestamp unchanged if a later operation reverts, so there exist fuzzed inputs (a batcherHash pointing to a contract that reverts when called) that make the mutant differ.

For any caller equal to DEPOSITOR_ACCOUNT and any input values, calling setL1BlockValues successfully updates the public timestamp to the provided _timestamp; the mutant that requires msg.sender==address(0) prevents the legitimate depositor from updating timestamp, so for some fuzzed depositor address equal to the contract's DEPOSITOR_ACCOUNT the reference sets timestamp while the mutant leaves it unchanged.
Only the designated depositor account can change the stored basefee via setL1BlockValues

For any inputs passed to setL1BlockValues, the reference contract stores basefee exactly equal to the provided _basefee; the mutant stores basefee != _basefee for inputs where _basefee + 1 != _basefee (i.e., any _basefee not equal to type(uint256).max), so the invariant is violated for many fuzzed values.

For every input to setL1BlockValues, the reference contract stores basefee equal to the provided _basefee; the mutant stores basefee = _basefee + 1 for most inputs, thereby violating that equality for any _basefee where _basefee + 1 != _basefee (i.e. all values except uint256.max).

For any inputs to setL1BlockValues, the reference contract stores the provided _basefee into the public basefee variable (c.basefee() == _basefee); the mutant overwrites basefee with 0 so this equality can be violated for some fuzzed _basefee != 0.

For any inputs and when called by the depositor, setL1BlockValues stores the provided _hash into the public hash state variable; the mutant instead always writes a fixed constant, so there exist inputs where c.hash() != provided _hash (the reference preserves the input hash but the mutant does not).

For any inputs and when called by the depositor account, C.hash() equals the provided _hash after setL1BlockValues; the mutant stores hash XORed with a constant so for some _hash values the stored hash differs.

For any inputs to setL1BlockValues, the reference contract always stores the provided _hash value into its public hash() slot (so c.hash() == _hash after the call); the mutant that reorders the assignment can cause c.hash() != _hash for some inputs (due to a storage-write reordering observable when writes overlap with other storage slots), so the invariant c.hash() == _hash is violated for some fuzzed inputs.

For every call to setL1BlockValues, the correct contract stores the provided _hash such that c.hash() == _hash; the mutant that moves the hash assignment may cause c.hash() != _hash for some inputs, so the property c.hash() == _hash distinguishes them.

For every call to setL1BlockValues by the depositor, the contract's public hash getter returns exactly the _hash argument passed; the mutant that reorders the assignment can for some combinations of inputs (when storage slot write ordering interacts with overlapping calldata/state patterns) result in c.hash() != _hash.

For every admissible call by the depositor, after setL1BlockValues returns the public getter hash() equals the _hash argument; the mutant that moves the hash assignment can cause hash() to differ from the supplied _hash for some fuzzed inputs, so asserting c.hash() == _hash distinguishes them.

For every admissible call to setL1BlockValues by the depositor, the public getter `hash()` equals the calldata argument `_hash` after the call; the mutant's reordered assignment can cause `hash()` to differ for some calldata/slot patterns, so asserting equality distinguishes them.
